text: @stmol/dsh-rub-cost（DSH 网页插件）：在 DeepSeek Harness 对话栏显示当前会话的卢布费用。它将交互按钮接入 conversation.composer.dock，并从主会话的 tokenUsage 与最近使用模型估算费用。面板展示当前模型、峰谷 тариф及切换倒计时、美元单价、卢布汇率、缓存节省、子代理合计和 DeepSeek 钱包余额。适合想快速了解会话开销的 DeepSeek Harness 用户；不需 API Key，余额显示需连接 DeepSeek 账户。

@stmol/dsh-rub-cost estimates DSH session cost in rubles from token usage and the last used model. A dock button opens a panel with tariff, exchange rate, cache savings, subagent total, and DeepSeek wallet balances. No API key is needed; wallet balances require a connected account.
想在 DSH 对话栏直接看到当前会话花了多少卢布。
有没有办法查看 DeepSeek 会话费用并按当前汇率换算？
让 DSH 显示模型当前的峰时或非峰时单价。
我想知道缓存命中大约省下了多少会话费用。
怎样把子代理的花费也合并到会话总额里查看？
能在对话页面顺便查看 DeepSeek 钱包余额吗？
Show me an estimate of my current DeepSeek session spend in rubles.
I want to see the active model tariff and when its pricing window changes.
@stmol/dsh-rub-cost 的功能「会话费用」：根据 tokenUsage、最近使用的模型及当前峰谷费率估算会话美元成本，再按卢布汇率换算；金额显示在对话栏按钮和弹出的费用卡片中。
@stmol/dsh-rub-cost 的功能「费用明细」：点击对话栏金额打开面板，可查看模型费率、峰谷切换倒计时、汇率、无缓存成本与缓存节省。
@stmol/dsh-rub-cost 的功能「子代理费用合计」：面板打开时读取子代理会话用量并定期刷新，将可计价的子代理费用加入单独的合计行。
@stmol/dsh-rub-cost 的功能「DeepSeek 钱包余额」：插件挂载和每次打开费用面板时读取账户余额，并在面板列出钱包与非零奖励余额。
@stmol/dsh-rub-cost 使用前须知：卢布换算依赖 www.cbr-xml-daily.ru 的汇率数据；成功获取的汇率会缓存在浏览器中，网络刷新失败时沿用上次结果。

@stmol/dsh-rub-cost README · dsh-rub-cost：A DeepSeek Harness plugin: it shows the cost of the current session in rubles in
the conversation dock, next to the built-in token counters
(`conversation.composer.dock`).

@stmol/dsh-rub-cost README · dsh-rub-cost：The pill is a button. Clicking it opens a card styled after the built-in "Token
usage" popover; a second click, a click outside the card, or Escape closes it.
During peak hours the ruble amount on the pill is printed in amber — the same
warning colour the tariff row uses.

@stmol/dsh-rub-cost README · Installation：Published on npm as [`@stmol/dsh-rub-cost`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@stmol/dsh-rub-cost).
Any DSH bundle source works: an npm package, a Git repository, a tarball, or a
local folder.

* **GUI:** Settings → Plugins → Add plugin, then `@stmol/dsh-rub-cost`, or the
  [repository](https://github.com/Stmol/dsh-rub-cost) address.
* **CLI:** `dsh plugin add @stmol/dsh-rub-cost`.

@stmol/dsh-rub-cost README · Installation：The install name is the `name` field in `package.json`; the `name` in
`cordis.patch.yml` and the factory `id` in `client.js` have to match it, or the
bundle will not build. There are no automatic updates: remove the plugin and add
it again. The plugin runs with your own privileges.

@stmol/dsh-rub-cost README · What the card shows：Model, the current tariff and the countdown to its switch, the API price list in
dollars per 1M output tokens at the tariff in effect,
the CBR rate with its publication date, the cost of the session including
subagents, the same session without a cache and the savings, and the DeepSeek
Platform wallet balances. The session cost itself is the ruble amount on the pill
and in the card header; the card does not repeat it in dollars.

@stmol/dsh-rub-cost README · What the card shows：Peak hours cost twice the off-peak rate. The tariff row names only the window in
effect, for example `peak hours (04:00-07:00)` highlighted in amber, or
`off-peak`. Peak hours are Beijing weekdays 09:00-12:00 and 14:00-18:00, printed
in your browser's timezone — 04:00-07:00 and 09:00-13:00 at UTC+3, and the same
windows shifted by your own offset; weekends are off-peak around the
clock. The tariff itself is never computed in your zone: the rule stays in
Beijing time, and only the printed clock moves, so the amount is the same
wherever the card is opened. The countdown follows from that rule alone, so on a
Friday it runs into the next week: `63h 00m` just after 13:00 MSK, `61h 47m` at
14:13 MSK. The rule assumes the following Monday is an ordinary working day; a
PRC holiday moves the real switch, as the first limitation below explains.

@stmol/dsh-rub-cost README · How it is computed：`cost = (uncachedInput + cacheWrite) × cacheMiss + cacheRead × cacheHit + output × output`

Tokens are priced with DeepSeek's official dollar list per 1M tokens, then
converted at the CBR USD/RUB rate. The account is billed in dollars, so the
dollar list is the basis; the yuan list on the Chinese documentation page is the
same list at the fixed 20/3 ¥/$ rate. A usage report can show amounts in CNY
while a granted yuan balance is being spent, which is that same list again.

@stmol/dsh-rub-cost README · How it is computed：Tokens come from the host `tokenUsage` projection and the model from
`modelSelection.lastUsed`; the plugin never folds the session journal itself. The
price rows print the same model's `MODEL_PRICES` entry for the tariff in effect,
so they move only when the tariff or the model does. The rate comes from a mirror
of the CBR rates and is cached in `localStorage`: with no network the last known
rate is used, and with no cache the cell shows a dash and the reason in the
tooltip.

@stmol/dsh-rub-cost README · How it is computed：The pill and the card header are a running total: the cost of the current session,
not of the account and not a per-request price. Subagents are priced from their
own route and summed into a separate "Total with subagents" row; while the card is
open their spend is polled every 15 seconds. If even one child cannot be read, that
row is hidden rather than shown incomplete.

@stmol/dsh-rub-cost README · Known limitations：* PRC statutory holidays are not modelled. The plugin keeps one year-agnostic
  rule — Beijing weekday plus peak window — so it needs no annual edit, and a
  holiday weekday is therefore priced as a peak day. DeepSeek bills those days at
  the off-peak rate, so on such a day the amount and the countdown are both too
  high until the holiday is over. The official dates live in the State Council
  notice published every November, which is the only source; the client bundle
  ships no year-specific table on purpose.
* The ruble total is not a sum of per-request bills: the whole session is repriced
  at the tariff in effect when the card renders, so a peak/off-peak switch doubles
  or halves the amount without a single new token. The tariff and the price rows
  name what is in effect, which is exactly what the countdown counts down to.
* `tokenUsage` holds a whole-session total with no per-route split, so after a
  mid-session model change everything is estimated with the last used model.
* Cache writes are billed at the cache miss rate: DeepSeek publishes no separate
  price, and on DeepSeek routes that counter is zero anyway.
